decisions.reason: The existing message-539 MODIFY already limits owner discovery to NFTs from the active replacement contract and excludes legacy-contract NFTs.
The existing message-539 MODIFY already excludes legacy-contract NFTs from active dashboard rendering while preserving the independent media-presentation rules.
The existing message-539 MODIFY already restricts ownership-gated book access to NFTs from the active replacement contract.
The existing message-539 MODIFY already limits metadata used by the active system to the replacement contract and excludes legacy-contract metadata.
The existing message-539 MODIFY already records replacement-contract-only platform statistics, exclusion of legacy activity, and the fresh prize-draw state described in the accepted proposal.
This requirement already has a message-539 INTRODUCE that directly records the accepted fresh-state migration policy; an additional propagated MODIFY would duplicate it.
The existing message-539 MODIFY already redirects the USDC mint flow to the active replacement contract.
Using a fresh replacement contract does not alter the established semantics for book access, referral identity, badges, or ticket state when an active NFT is transferred.
The accepted fresh-contract policy necessarily excludes referral, ticket, and payout reporting derived from old-contract NFTs from the active dashboard.

decisions.reason: The migration decision does not necessarily change any current About-page copy or its documented prize and product explanations.

The accepted loss of old-contract copies may make the requested transfer of token IDs 17, 31, and 46 obsolete, but the supplied evidence does not establish that those IDs are legacy-contract NFTs or explicitly cancel their transfer.
Any future Transak mint must create its NFT through the active replacement contract because the client accepted that old-contract NFTs will not be used by the active system.
